title: Compatibility Negotiation Window & Semantic Versioning Policy for Serving Runtime
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Purpose:
Establish a single, operationally practical semantic versioning policy for the serving runtime that centers a Compatibility Negotiation Window: an explicit, observable period during which a server-side change that would otherwise be breaking can be advertised, exercised, and automatically mitigated while downstream clients migrate. This ticket captures definitions, timelines, headers/telemetry contracts, rollout gates, and upgrade-tooling requirements needed to implement the negotiation window across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Key principles (high level):
- Breaking changes must be explicit and rare. Default compatibility is backward-compatible for requests made under an older declared client contract.
- Additive, non-behavioral changes are minor/patch; changes that alter response semantics or remove fields are major unless covered by the negotiation window and mitigation tooling.
- Deprecation should be observable: runtime emits advisories and a deprecation grace window before enforcement.
- Provide automated shims and a compatibility test harness so teams can ship change with low operational risk.

Definitions (non-ambiguous):
- Compatible change: any change that preserves documented output semantics for existing client requests.
- Soft-deprecation: server indicates a field/option will be removed; server continues to honor old behavior for the negotiation window period.
- Breaking change: any change that causes previously valid requests to fail or return materially different output quality without a mitigation layer.
- Negotiation window: a minimum time interval (default 90 days) where soft-deprecations and reversible breaking behaviors are advertised and compatibility mitigations are active.

Versioning rules (semantic mapping):
- MAJOR increments: true incompatible changes after negotiation window without mitigation; also used for end-of-life of a compatibility layer.
- MINOR increments: additive features and non-breaking opt-in behaviors; can introduce new response fields behind feature flags.
- PATCH increments: bug fixes and internal optimizations with no external behavioral change.

Negotiation window lifecycle (recommended defaults):
1) Announcement (T0): change is documented in release notes and compatibility advisories; runtime starts emitting advisory headers for all requests: "X-RW-Compat-Advisory: v<old>->v<new>" and a machine-readable header "X-RW-Compat-Deadline: YYYY-MM-DD".
2) Observability (T0+2w): telemetry shows adoption and compatibility test results; any high error signals pause the rollout.
3) Migration window (T0 -> T0+90d): clients upgrade. Runtime continues honoring old requests and may emit warnings in response bodies when legacy fields are used.
4) Enforcement plan (after 90d): if adoption >= 95% and no high-severity regressions, enforce and bump MAJOR. Otherwise extend window, add canary steps, or ship automated shim.

Rollout gates and automation:
- Canary gates: region-based canaries with automatic rollback if token-level error rate or latency percentile deteriorates beyond configured SLO deltas.
- Telemetry gates: compatibility-test pass rate, error-rate delta, and model-quality delta (for generated-text changes) feed a rule engine that can pause enforcement.
- Emergency rollback: enable a single-step revert path by preserving previous model/binary image and restoring compatibility headers that route traffic to older runtime image for affected customers.

Client-server signalling and headers: (operator-facing API)
- Clients SHOULD send "X-RW-Client-Version: runtime-compat@<semver>" to declare the contract they expect.
- Servers MUST emit "X-RW-Compat-Advisory" and "X-RW-Compat-Deadline" when starting a negotiation window.
- Servers MAY return "X-RW-Compat-Score: <0-100>" indicating automated compatibility-check confidence for the client's usage pattern.
- For long-running migrations, servers MAY provide a link in header "X-RW-Compat-Details: <URL>" to a migration guide.

Deprecation policy and timelines: (examples)
- Field removal: announce -> 90d negotiation window -> enforcement; accelerate only with opt-in and customer consent.
- Behavioral change (model output differences): longer window (180d) with evaluation-based rollout because downstream quality regressions can be subtle.
- Performance-only changes (latency improvements): patch-level unless they alter observable tokenization or output ordering.

Tooling required (minimum viable):
- compat-validator (CLI): static diff and runtime smoke tests against canned prompt suites; outputs a "compat-score" and a human-friendly report.
- compat-shim-generator: auto-generate adapter code for simple field renames and schema layering for SDKs.
- runtime-telemetry-advisor: dashboards and rule engine that compute pass/fail for rollout gates and feed the rollout controller.
- amcli / rollout API extension: allow release managers to start a negotiation-window release that wires advisory headers, schedules canaries, and tracks adoption metrics.

Acceptance criteria (must be met before marking Done):
- Policy document published in docs/runtime/semver-negotiation.md and linked from release notes.
- compat-validator CLI implemented with at least the following checks: schema-preservation, endpoint smoke tests, and golden-output delta.
- Runtime emits required headers when a negotiation window is active.
- Rollout controller has an automated gate that blocks enforcement if error-rate or quality regressions detected.
- A migration guide template is available and used in two pilot rollouts.

Implementation plan (phases):
- Phase 1 (2 sprints): policy doc, header contracts, and rollout controller stub; first-pass compat-validator prototype.
- Phase 2 (3 sprints): compat-shim-generator, telemetry advisor dashboards, and rollout playbooks for SRE/product.
- Phase 3 (1 sprint): pilot rollout for a low-risk change (docs-only or additive field) to validate the negotiation window end-to-end.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: clients ignore headers and remain on old SDKs. Mitigation: console-level alerts, emailed subscriber lists, and forced display in tenant console with explicit action required for Private deployments.
- Risk: subtle quality regressions not caught by smoke tests. Mitigation: require small-scale A/B evaluation for model-behavior changes and include human-eval spot checks in rollout gates.
- Risk: negotiation windows too long create maintenance burden. Mitigation: allow case-by-case shorter windows for low-impact non-behavioral changes with documented justification.

Docs and links (authoritative):
- Migration guide template: https://confluence.redwood/internal/runtime/negotiation-window-template
- Compat-validator repo (proto): https://github.com/redwood-inference/compat-validator
- Rollout controller design doc: https://confluence.redwood/internal/runtime/rollout-controller-design

Operational notes for SRE/Support:
- Support playbook must include a quick command to toggle advisory headers and route traffic to the previous runtime in <5m.
- Incident postmortem must capture whether negotiation-window signals (compat-score, telemetry) were sufficient and recommend changes if not.

Next steps:
- Review with PM and Legal for any customer-communication constraints (deadline wording, required notice).
- Build prototype of compat-validator and emit header in a behind-the-flag runtime build for internal testing.
